title: F-gas equipment leak-check and recordkeeping QA controls

sources.title: Checking F gas equipment for leaks
Record F gas in equipment you own or service

facts.source_fact: Leak-check duties cover specified stationary refrigeration, air-conditioning, heat-pump, fire-protection, refrigerated truck/trailer, switchgear and organic Rankine equipment.
Responsibility for preventing F-gas leaks is shared between equipment users and service technicians.
Leak-check frequency depends on the amount of F gas and its global warming potential expressed as CO2 equivalent.
Equipment containing 5 to less than 50 tonnes CO2 equivalent generally requires checks at least every 12 months.
Equipment containing 50 to less than 500 tonnes CO2 equivalent generally requires checks at least every 6 months.
Certain equipment at 500 tonnes CO2 equivalent or more has more frequent or automatic leak-detection requirements.
Installing automatic leak detection can double the permitted interval between leak checks where the rule applies.
Automatic leak detection is required for specified equipment containing 500 tonnes CO2 equivalent or more, subject to listed exceptions.
Leak-detection systems must alert the operator or responsible service company when a leak is detected.
Leak-detection systems on most covered equipment must be checked every year.
Leak-detection systems on electrical switchgear are checked every 6 years under the stated rule.
A detected F-gas leak must be repaired as soon as possible.
After repair, the equipment must be retested within one month to confirm the repair worked.
Failure to carry out required leak checks or repair leaks can lead to civil penalties.
Records must be kept for covered equipment containing F gas equivalent to 5 tonnes or more of CO2.
Required F-gas equipment records must be retained for 5 years.
Records include the quantity and type of gas in the equipment when installed.
Records include quantity and type of gas added during maintenance such as leak repair.
Records include dates and results of all mandatory leak checks.
Records include what was done to recover and dispose of gas and relevant service or waste-carrier information.

guard_patterns.handling: Preserve the equipment rule and threshold.
Attach equipment type and CO2e threshold.
Attach guidance version and service dates.
Carry leak-check, repair and record-retention evidence.
Do not convert equipment records into parcel emissions.
